clue.text: Joint with soft drink brought round: thanks for the snack

indicators.note: the drink is wrapped around the joint, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink
the hip is a joint of the body
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone takes a joint, a cola is passed round, and they say thanks for the nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a cut of meat or a spliff, but it is the body part. A chipolata is a small thin British sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata, a small cocktail sausage, is commonly eaten as a party nibble or light bite.

clue.text: Realise Daisy is a source of easy money

parts.note: to realise an asset is to cash it, turn it into money
Daisy is a traditional name for a cow

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that Daisy brings in money without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realise' reads as 'understand' but means convert to money, CASH; Daisy is the stock name for a dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably earns profit with little further investment.

clue.text: Tidy home, given command

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A household is told to tidy up, and it is an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in order is neatly arranged, which is what tidy describes.

clue.text: How one might make the bar, panting

definitions.text: How one might make the bar
definitions.meaning: the letters of BAR and THE come out of the word BREATH, so you make them from its letters

explanation.surface: Someone arrives gasping at the pub, having rushed to get there.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: rearranging the letters of BREATH gives THE BAR, so 'the bar' is made out of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of breath means gasping for air, exactly the state of someone panting.

clue.text: The sort of letters one finds in a crossword

definitions.text: The sort of letters one finds in a crossword

parts.words: The sort of letters one finds in a crossword
parts.note: many crossword clues give letters to be sorted, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A plain description of what fills a crossword grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' is the key: these are letters waiting to be sorted into order, the commonest clue device of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made by rearranging the letters of another is the basis of a whole family of cryptic clues.

clue.text: Close and commonly bald

indicators.note: common speech drops the aitch at the start of words, so the leading H falls away

parts.note: hairless means bald

explanation.surface: Someone is described as near and, in plain words, bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is the weather sense, stuffy, not 'near'. 'commonly' drops the H as in Cockney speech: 'AIRLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather or a close room is muggy and stuffy, lacking fresh moving air.

clue.text: Trophy I had as boy archer

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the trophy they won as a young archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid, the Roman god of love, is pictured as a winged boy with bow and arrows.

clue.text: Endlessly chilly in depression

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: cold means chilly

explanation.surface: Someone feels perpetually cold and low in spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood; it is a dip between mountain peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks, a hollow or saddle in the land.

clue.text: Biographical sketch is for dossier

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a dossier is a file

explanation.surface: A short biography is destined for someone's records.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a short written portrait of a person's life and character.

clue.text: Dance, heartlessly frivolous pleasure

indicators.note: with its heart gone only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: light means frivolous, not serious

explanation.surface: A dance offering carefree, empty-hearted fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' strips Dance to its outer letters, DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great pleasure or joy.

clue.text: The nose one looks down?

parts.note: a snob looks down their nose at others, and this informal word for nose gives the word for such snobbery

explanation.surface: A question about which nose a person gazes along.
explanation.walkthrough: Looking down one's nose means being snobbish; this nose is the root of 'snooty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snoot is a slang term for the nose, and it also gives 'snooty', meaning haughty.

clue.text: One day this person will be caught out

definitions.text: One day this person will be caught out

parts.words: One day this person will be caught out
parts.note: on one particular day of the year people are tricked by pranks, and the victim gets this name

explanation.surface: A prediction that a deceiver's luck will eventually run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One day' sounds like 'eventually'; it is a specific day, the first of April.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim of a prank played on the first of April is given this name by tradition.

clue.text: Fake medic turned away

indicators.note: turned round so the word reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: doc is short for doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A bogus doctor is shown the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod as an adjective is British informal for mock or sham, as in a cod accent.

clue.text: Sweeping, managing to cover stretch of river

indicators.note: one word covers the other, so it is placed around it

parts.note: faring means getting on, managing
a reach is a straight stretch of a river

explanation.surface: Someone cleans broadly, trying to cover a length of riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweeping' looks like housework; it means wide-ranging. FAR(REACH)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-reaching changes are sweeping ones, having wide and extensive effect.

clue.text: A good hand graphically represented

indicators.note: presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fine handwriting shown in pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' reorders GRAPHICALLY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful handwriting, and a hand is a style of writing.

clue.text: One's beaten by hostile tribe

parts.note: the thing struck by warriors preparing to fight is an instrument, not a defeated enemy

explanation.surface: Someone is defeated by an enemy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' suggests defeat; it means struck, as a drum is.
explanation.definitionFit: A war drum is a drum struck to summon or rally warriors before battle.

clue.text: Prominent foreigner in the way

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: A conspicuous foreigner is blocking someone's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the way' reads as obstructing, but 'in' is the container signal and 'the way' is the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Something salient stands out and is most noticeable or important.

clue.text: The start of everything, a very noisy affair?

definitions.meaning: the theorised event that began the universe
taken literally, a huge loud bang

explanation.surface: The universe's beginning was surely a loud event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is the cosmological event from which the universe began, and literally a giant explosion.

clue.text: Ship with pirate

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
and means with, together

explanation.surface: A vessel and its buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pirate' here is the robber, not a sea raider specifically.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit or robber, a near synonym of pirate as lawless plunderer.

clue.text: Serious expert's dissatisfied look

parts.note: grim means serious, stern
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A solemn specialist frowns in displeasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression showing disgust or displeasure.

clue.text: One picking up scraps in general mess

indicators.note: a mess is a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gathers leftovers in the officers' dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general mess' suggests an army canteen; 'mess' jumbles GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers leftover grain after a harvest, or collects bits of information.

clue.text: Quarrelsome when talking in takeaway shop

indicators.note: spoken out loud, a word with the same sound is meant

parts.note: chippy means touchy, easily provoked

explanation.surface: Someone gets argumentative while chatting in a fast food outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A chippie is British slang for a fish and chip shop, a classic takeaway.

clue.text: Easy shot, we hear, over key stronghold

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece stands over, before, the next
said out loud, a word with the same sound is meant

parts.note: a sitter is an easy shot or chance
Del is the delete key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A simple shot, it seems, at a vital fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a non-rhotic accent, where the final R of the easy shot is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, typically commanding a city, so a stronghold.

clue.text: Piece of Bach, perhaps: leave it alone to start with

parts.note: to part is to leave, depart

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to leave a piece of Bach well alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a suite of instrumental movements, a form Bach wrote for violin and keyboard.

clue.text: Approve of Red Nose fooling

indicators.note: fooling about puts these letters into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Backing the clowning of Red Nose Day, a British charity comedy fundraiser.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to give it approval or support.

clue.text: Brendan and his dog?

definitions.meaning: Brendan is a Guardian crossword compiler, here pictured as Irish

explanation.surface: A man named Brendan and the dog he owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is both a crossword compiler and a dog; Brendan is a fellow Guardian setter and a classic Irish name.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish setter is a dog breed, and an Irish crossword compiler is literally one too.

clue.text: Stick parts of biro delicately together

indicators.note: only portions of the following words are used, so the letters are hidden inside them
the two words are run together so their adjoining parts can be read as one

explanation.surface: Instructions to glue a pen's pieces back carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' sounds like glue; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a thin straight stick or bar.

clue.text: Finished in a group, so left alone

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians
done means finished

explanation.surface: A musician's run in a band is over, so they are deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished in a group' reads as one idea, but 'in' places the first word inside the following two.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abandoned is to be deserted, left by others on one's own.

clue.text: Dorothy comes to a full stop

definitions.meaning: A short form of the name Dorothy
a full stop, the punctuation mark

explanation.surface: Dorothy halts completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a pet form of Dorothy and also a small point such as a full stop.

clue.text: Was he just a monk before?

definitions.meaning: a monk ranking just below an abbot, or heading a priory

explanation.surface: Was this senior cleric once an ordinary monk?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on promotion: was the prior just a monk before?
explanation.definitionFit: A prior is a monastic superior, and prior as an adjective means earlier in time.

clue.text: Having lived, died with mark of beating

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
a welt is a raised mark left by a blow

explanation.surface: An obituary: someone lived, died, and bore the scars of beatings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past form of dwell, to live or reside somewhere.

clue.text: All but one of the team drop out of this

definitions.text: All but one of the team drop out of this

parts.words: All but one of the team drop out of this
parts.note: each runner hands over and stops, so only the final team member finishes, rather than quitting

explanation.surface: A sporting event where nearly the whole team quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop out' suggests giving up; each member simply finishes their leg and passes the baton.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay race team members run in turn, each stopping after handing over the baton.
